newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea agrees to return submarine crew bodies.
newsitem.headline: South Korea agrees to return submarine crew bodies.

text.p: South Korea will send home the bodies of North Koreans shot after landing from a submarine in September if Pyongyang makes a request, the defence ministry said on Monday.
Earlier, the United Nations Command said it may conduct a "repatriation of remains" ceremony as early as Monday afternoon.

The move comes a day after Pyongyang apologised for the incursion of the submarine that set ashore 26 infiltrators. Twenty-four intruders were killed, one was captured and another is still on the loose.
A defence ministry official, who declined to be named, said South Korea would not return the captured agent or the submarine as Pyongyang has demanded.
Nevertheless, handing back the remains clears the last major problem from the submarine incident that raised military tensions on the Korean peninsula.
The bodies would be sent home via the border crossing point of Panmunjom.

"Since North Korea has officially apologised and promised to prevent a recurrence of such incidents we have decided to return the bodies through appropriate channels if North Korea makes a request," a defence ministry statement said.
"We look forward to North Korea's cooperation towards peace and stability on the Korean peninsula."
The U.S.-led United Nations Command monitors a ceasefire that ended the 1950-53 Korean War. It is the primary channel of communication between the two Koreas.
